subject.title: [Bug]: Task and Memory Recall Is Often Too Weak to Trust Across Real Conversations

question: What default memory/task recall contract should OpenClaw support for project and task state across fresh sessions and mutations?
rationale: The remaining work is not one known bug path; it requires a product/security choice about default memory behavior, transcript visibility, Active Memory use, and whether project/task state should be a core convention, plugin mode, or documented workspace pack.

options.title: Define a core reliability contract
options.body: Specify the minimum default behavior for remembering project/task state, current focus, open-only task queries, and live gate acceptance before implementation begins.

options.title: Route to an opt-in memory mode
options.body: Keep defaults conservative and sponsor a default-off Active Memory or workspace-pack mode with explicit privacy and upgrade documentation.

options.title: Split diagnostics only
options.body: Open a narrower issue for session-id/cache-key error classification and leave project/task memory behavior for a later roadmap decision.

recommendation.title: Define a core reliability contract
recommendation.body: Specify the minimum default behavior for remembering project/task state, current focus, open-only task queries, and live gate acceptance before implementation begins.

likelyOwner.reason: The session-memory source and default memory-search configuration history point to Peter Steinberger as the best available routing owner for the default contract decision.
